messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired: LR-LB-EDGE-PROD (severity: P1) — multiple TLS handshake failures + LB target unhealthy. PD: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345 — auto-escalate in 5m unless acked.

aj: @channel acked — oncall here, looking into handshake spike and target health. :raised_hand:

oncall-sre: Joining. Maria, can you pull the last 30m from edge metrics and confirm customer impact?

maria: pulling now. quick summary: TLS handshake errors (SNI/TLS_ALERT) starting 2026-07-11T17:03 UTC, spike ~18x, LB 5xx from targets up. Probe shows some regions resolving to new-edge IPs where cert rotation completed ~17:00.

maria: Snippet from probe run:```bash
$ curl -v https://edge.example.com/health
* Connected to edge.example.com (203.0.113.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: SSL routines:tls_construct_server_key_exchange:wrong version number
```

aj: I'm triaging; starting failover to secondary pool per runbook (edge-failover). ETA ~2m.

pagerduty-bot: Acknowledgement recorded by aj. Escalation timers paused.

oncall-sre: Looks like the new pool has a cert mismatch — cert rotated to CN that doesn't match SNI for legacy hostnames. DNS TTL for the A record was 300s; some clients still hitting new IPs. Options: rollback cert on new pool OR re-route traffic to legacy cert pool. Which is faster?

sam: I can rollback cert on new pool within ~4m. Risk: new cert had SANs for extra hostnames, but rollback small window ok. If we reroute, need to update LB config and may cause brief connection churn. I'd prefer cert rollback to keep routing intact.

elaine: Support seeing 4 customer reports so far, mainly EU and APAC. I'll update the status page once we have mitigation progress.

aj: Executing failover command now:```bash
edge-ctl failover --to secondary-pool --reason "handshake spike / cert mismatch"
# started at 2026-07-11T17:07:12Z
```

incident-bot: Auto-escalation timer canceled (ack by aj).

maria: Post-failover quick metrics: EU TLS errors 18 -> 3, NA 22 -> 5, APAC 30 -> 12 (still elevated due to DNS caches). Latency stable, 5xxs declining.

oncall-sre: Good improvement. Next steps: 1) sam roll back cert on new pool 2) keep failover for 30m 3) monitor DNS propagation for APAC caches. If stable at 30m we can begin de-escalation.

sam: Rolling back cert now:```bash
certsctl rollback --pool new-edge --version v2026-07-10
# completed 2026-07-11T17:10:02Z
```

sam: Verified from test nodes:```bash
$ curl -I https://edge.example.com
* Connected to edge.example.com (198.51.100.22) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), Cipher is TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

elaine: Status page updated: "Partial degradation — we are mitigating an issue affecting TLS handshakes for a subset of clients. Engineers are working on a fix." I'll keep customers posted in 20m.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by aj at 2026-07-11T17:08:30Z. Current status: mitigation in progress.

oncall-sre: Can we avoid lowering DNS TTL globally? Lowering makes future changes propagate faster but adds churn. For now we'll keep TTL and let caches expire; APAC will clear in ~TTL.

maria: Metrics show steady decline for last 10m; APAC error rate trending down.

aj: Starting de-escalation run: if stable for next 15m we will close PD and open postmortem ticket. Creating RCA ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-4521 — assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

elaine: I'll draft customer comms and attach impact list (4 customers, request ids).

maria: Final checks at 17:28 UTC — TLS errors back to baseline in EU/NA, APAC baseline within 12m. No remaining 5xx spikes.

aj: Closing PD incident. Marking incident as mitigated; postmortem to follow. Thanks all. :tada:

incident-bot: Incident closed by aj at 2026-07-11T17:30:20Z. PD incident PD12345 closed.
